correctness.rationale: The theorem is proved for every finite \(n\ge2\) from explicit definitions. Sufficiency follows from independence of the iid-prefix rank permutation and order statistics. Necessity uses an exact likelihood-ratio monotonicity lemma whose derivative is controlled by convexity/concavity of \(u\mapsto u^x\), giving the covariance sign and an induction over \(k\). Exact Laplace-transform identities independently check the event probabilities. No numerical evidence is used to infer an infinite or universal statement.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete finite-sample classification in the canonical heterogeneous exponential family, not merely another counterexample. It identifies exactly which scale perturbations preserve finite record-indicator independence and gives a directional adjacent-covariance law that explains a one-step detection delay. This sharpens the prior qualitative statement that heterogeneous exponential indicators are dependent in general and provides a precise diagnostic boundary for record-based trend/change analyses.
